topic.title: Privacy-Preserving Inference and Information Leakage
topic.overview: This topic studies how information about users or training data can leak through learned systems and how to limit that exposure. Papers examine encrypted inference, collaborative representations, gradient reconstruction, private training, and unlearning. A representative framework connects a network's local sensitivity to formal privacy guarantees for representations shared with an inference provider.
topic.whyItMatters: Failure of one reconstruction attack does not prove privacy. Formal guarantees, realistic threat models, and targeted leakage tests address different parts of the problem, including risks introduced by an untrusted pretrained model or by residual information after unlearning.
topic.evolution: The representatives begin with privacy-preserving face detection, encrypted networks, and verifiable execution. Later work studies gradient leakage and posthoc privacy. Recent research scrutinizes corrupted model supply chains, hidden unlearning leakage, and fine-grained visual privacy detection in images and streams.
openQuestions: How can privacy guarantees remain meaningful when pretrained components are untrusted?
Which evaluations reveal sensitive information that ordinary utility or forgetting metrics overlook?

papers.title: Deep Learning with Plausible Deniability
papers.tldr: PD-SGD probabilistically rejects training updates that fail plausible deniability, offering theoretical privacy protection and a favorable empirical privacy–utility trade-off.

papers.title: DictPFL: Efficient and Private Federated Learning on Encrypted Gradients
papers.tldr: DictPFL makes encrypted federated training substantially cheaper by keeping a static dictionary local and encrypting a pruned, updatable lookup table.

papers.title: Factor Decorrelation Enhanced Data Removal from Deep Predictive Models
papers.tldr: The method combines feature decorrelation and loss perturbation to protect information during data removal while preserving predictive performance.

papers.title: FracFace: Breaking the Visual Clues—Fractal-Based Privacy-Preserving Face Recognition
papers.tldr: FracFace refines and fractally remaps frequency features to reduce facial reconstruction while maintaining high recognition accuracy on evaluated benchmarks.

papers.title: Impact of Dataset Properties on Membership Inference Vulnerability of Deep Transfer Learning
papers.tldr: Membership-inference vulnerability falls with examples per class according to a power law, but the most exposed examples require very large datasets for adequate protection.

papers.title: LOMIA: Label-Only Membership Inference Attacks against Pre-trained Large Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: LOMIA infers potential training-data membership from vision-language models' top predictions without requiring their full prediction scores.

papers.title: LoRO: Real-Time on-Device Secure Inference for LLMs via TEE-Based Low Rank Obfuscation
papers.tldr: LoRO uses reusable low-rank factors to mask model parameters efficiently, reducing secure-memory and inference costs while resisting the evaluated model-stealing attack.

papers.title: More effort is needed to protect pedestrian privacy in the era of AI
papers.tldr: The paper calls for stronger pedestrian-data collection and anonymization practices that protect privacy while preserving research utility.

papers.title: ObCLIP: Oblivious CLoud-Device Hybrid Image Generation with Privacy Preservation
papers.tldr: ObCLIP hides a user's sensitive prompt choice among alternatives while splitting image generation between a large cloud model and a smaller local model.

papers.title: Obliviator Reveals the Cost of Nonlinear Guardedness in Concept Erasure
papers.tldr: Obliviator iteratively erases nonlinear attribute information while measuring and improving the trade-off between protection and task utility.

papers.title: PUO-Bench: A Panel Understanding and Operation Benchmark with A Privacy-Preserving Framework
papers.tldr: PUO-Bench tests physical control-panel understanding, while an edge–cloud framework reduces privacy risks by keeping raw images local.

papers.title: Secure and Confidential Certificates of Online Fairness
papers.tldr: OATH provides scalable, confidential group fairness certificates for data received during actual model deployment.

papers.title: The Unseen Threat: Residual Knowledge in Machine Unlearning under Perturbed Samples
papers.tldr: Perturbed forgotten samples can expose residual knowledge after unlearning; RURK targets this vulnerability through fine-tuning.

papers.title: Toward Efficient Inference Attacks: Shadow Model Sharing via Mixture-of-Experts
papers.tldr: SHAPOOL shares subnetworks across jointly trained shadow models to reduce membership-inference attack costs while maintaining comparable effectiveness.

papers.title: Adaptively Robust Resettable Streaming
papers.tldr: Dedicated sketches use differential privacy to support compact, adaptively robust summaries of streams whose values can increase or reset.

papers.title: An Empirical Study on the Resilience of Partial Merging to Model Clone Attacks
papers.tldr: Experiments show that partial model sharing can still expose private model capabilities to cloning attacks with limited prior knowledge.

papers.title: How Hard Can It Be? Hardness-Aware Multi-Objective Unlearning
papers.tldr: HAMU uses forget–retain similarity to guide unlearning and identify when preserving retained performance conflicts with forgetting.

papers.title: LMCleaner: Efficient and Certified Online Unlearning via Influence Propagation Truncation
papers.tldr: LMCleaner removes data influence during training using truncated influence tracking and calibrated noise, with certified approximate indistinguishability from retraining.

papers.title: MetaMoE: Diversity-Aware Proxy Selection for Privacy-Preserving Mixture-of-Experts Unification
papers.tldr: MetaMoE uses relevant, diverse public proxy data to coordinate private-domain experts and train a unified context-aware router.

papers.title: MultiPriv: Benchmarking Individual-Level Privacy Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: MultiPriv tests whether vision-language models can link scattered multimodal clues into individual profiles, revealing substantial capability in a controlled synthetic benchmark.

papers.title: OSNIP: Balancing the Privacy-Utility-Efficiency Trilemma in LLM Inference via Obfuscated Semantic Null Space
papers.tldr: OSNIP uses keyed client-side embedding perturbations to preserve semantic utility while sharply reducing attack success in reported evaluations.

papers.title: PISA: Privacy-Preserving Split Adaptation with Model IP Protection
papers.tldr: PISA combines split fine-tuning and utility-recovery methods to protect data and model IP, reporting a 23.0% GLUE gain over a privacy-focused baseline.

papers.title: Position: Embodied AI Requires a Privacy-Utility Tradeoff
papers.tldr: SPINE treats privacy as a dynamic constraint across the embodied AI life cycle, with preliminary cases illustrating effects across stages.

papers.title: Position: The Privacy-Auditability Paradox in Federated Learning: Why We Need Controllable Secure Aggregation
papers.tldr: The authors propose secure aggregation that hides updates by default but permits narrowly governed, consensus-bound audits of specific inputs.

papers.title: Position: Verifiable Data Minimization is a Prerequisite for Responsible, Privacy-Preserving Industrial Vision
papers.tldr: Industrial vision should verifiably minimize captured information to what a declared task needs, limiting opportunities for unauthorized inference.

papers.title: Privacy-Aware Video Anomaly Detection through Orthogonal Subspace Projection
papers.tldr: Guided orthogonal projection suppresses facial information in video representations while maintaining or improving anomaly-detection accuracy in experiments.

papers.title: PrivGate: Steering Contextual Integrity in LLMs via Latent Space Geometry
papers.tldr: PrivGate uses internal privacy signals to trigger reasoning selectively, reducing average privacy leakage by 62.6% relative with 15.9% token overhead.

papers.title: Provably Protecting Fine-Tuned LLMs from Training Data Extraction while Preserving Utility
papers.tldr: SCP-Δr smooths low-impact fine-tuning changes to strengthen extraction protection while preserving utility in the reported evaluations.

papers.title: Representation Unlearning: Forgetting through Information Compression
papers.tldr: Representation Unlearning learns an information-compressing transformation that suppresses forget-data information while preserving useful retained information.

papers.title: Revisiting ML Training under Fully Homomorphic Encryption: Convergence Guarantees, Differential Privacy, and Efficient Algorithms
papers.tldr: The paper analyzes convergence of encrypted training and introduces a more efficient differentially private algorithm tailored to FHE.

papers.title: SLIM: Secure and Efficient Inference for Large Language Models on Untrusted Devices via TEEs
papers.tldr: SLIM carries transformed representations across obfuscated layers to protect model weights with fewer TEE interactions and up to 13.80-fold faster inference.

papers.title: Source-Free Open-World RF Fingerprint Identification
papers.tldr: IO-ETF uses output geometry and multilevel alignment to balance new-device discovery with old-device retention when historical radio data cannot be stored.

papers.title: $\textttFHAIM$: Fully Homomorphic AIM for Private Tabular Synthetic Data Generation
papers.tldr: FHAIM trains a synthetic tabular-data generator on encrypted records and provides differential privacy for release while preserving AIM’s reported performance.

papers.title: The Double-Edged Nature of the Rashomon Set for Trustworthy Machine Learning
papers.tldr: Diverse near-optimal models support switching after attacks, but disclosing more of them increases training-data leakage.

papers.title: Unlearning Isn’t Forgetting: Revealing Hidden Leakage in Class Unlearning Evaluations
papers.tldr: A new attack exposes class information retained after unlearning, and TREW mitigates it by approximating retrained models’ remaining-class predictions.

papers.title: VPD-100K: Towards Generalizable and Fine-grained Visual Privacy Protection
papers.tldr: VPD-100K supplies detailed visual privacy annotations and a lightweight frequency-based module to improve detection of sensitive information in images and streams.
